fields.title: Evidence standard
fields.description: How should this QA goal prove its one end state — proof.txt containing the single line `status: ok`?

options.label: Host file + contains checks only (Recommended)
options.description: Two host-run criteria: a `file` check that proof.txt exists, and a `contains` check that its text holds `status: ok`. No human sign-off, no verifier/judge criterion, no budget. Fastest and fully deterministic.

options.value: Host checks plus an exactness command check
options.label: Host checks plus an exactness command check
options.description: Same file + contains checks, plus a `command` check that fails if the file has anything other than the single line. Stricter on exactness, but adds a shell command beyond the direct host checks you specified.

options.value: Host checks plus a verifier criterion
options.label: Host checks plus a verifier criterion
options.description: Adds a read-only verifier that must quote proof.txt. Costs an extra review round; you said no verifier criterion.

options.label: Host checks plus owner sign-off
options.description: Adds a `human` criterion requiring you to approve. Blocks automatic completion; you said no human sign-off.

answer.q0: Use the fixed QA choices: proof.txt = status: ok; direct host checks only, no verifier/human criterion, no budget, fresh root launch with the original model/agent.
